newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. DATA GIVES GERMAN SHARES LATE BOOST.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DATA GIVES GERMAN SHARES LATE BOOST.

text.p: German shares received a late boost on Friday afternoon from U.S. payrolls data which, while stronger than some had expected, allowed fears of an imminent United States rate hike to recede.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares had earlier closed 12.54 points lower at 2,517.0 as dealers cited heavy institutional short-selling before the figures.
But news that U.S. payrolls for August rose 250,000, compared to a consensus of forecasts around 244,000, was taken to mean that the U.S. Federal Reserve need not act immediately to tighten rates.

Taking its lead from higher early trading on Wall Street, the IBIS index of all-day electronic trade later moved up to close at 2,542.74, 10.19 points up on the day and far ahead of the day's low of 2,515.18.
"We've seen some short-selling that people are now deciding to cover," one dealer said, adding that he believed the selling had been overdone.
"It was still too speculative at this moment to start banking on a U.S. rate hike," he added.
September DAX futures traded 12 points higher at 2,547, joining the move upwards after a period of confusion directly after the U.S. data when prices on some traders screens were not appearing.
The Deutsche Boerse later confirmed that its DTB system had been unable to cope with the volume of business for a period of around five minutes.
With scheduled corporate news limited in the short-term, dealers said they expected the DAX to trade in a relatively tight range of between 2,500 to 2,550 until new impetus emerged.

Most DAX 30 shares traded higher on IBIS after the U.S. news but Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, was left 28 pfennigs lower at 72.12 on the electronic index on continued concern about its British-based Morgan Grenfell assest management arm.
Earlier on Friday the bank said it was seeking to overhaul its systems of controls after trading in three Morgan Grenfell funds was temporarily suspended over suspected irregularities.
